text: . Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), Chairman, Vivek Chaturvedi today inaugurated the GST and Customs Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) in New Delhi. Talking to the media, Mr Chaturvedi has said that the Customs Pavilion is largely focused on providing information about initiatives such as GST and Customs, which are recently undertaken by the government. He noted that the pavilion provides insights in relation to GST processes and the rate rationalisation exercise. The Chairman highlighted that dedicated helpdesks have also been set up to provide on-the-spot assistance to visitors on GST, Customs and related services.Finance Ministry said that the Pavilion is showcasing Next-Gen GST process reforms, updated Baggage Rules, 2026 and digital initiatives of CBIC.  It also highlighted that the dedicated helpdesks will provide a single-point interface for public assistance and facilitates direct interaction between the Department and citizens. To make awareness more interactive and engaging, the Pavilion features a range of innovative educational and entertainment activities for visitors across age groups.The Pavilion is also showcasing the Department’s digital transformation initiatives while highlighting the role of technology in promoting transparency, efficiency and ease of compliance

. India’s Wholesale Price Index (WPI) based inflation rose to 12.29 per cent in October on an annual basis, from 11.39 per cent in September. According to the provisional data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, crude petroleum and natural gas, mineral oils, basic metals, chemicals and chemical products were among the key drivers of wholesale price inflation during the month.Among the major categories in WPI, year-on-year inflation in the Fuel and Power surged sharply to 32.84 per cent last month. Inflation in Primary Articles rose to 9.24 per cent, from 8.67 per cent in September, while inflation in Manufactured Products eased marginally to 9.54 per cent during the same period. However, the WPI Food Index, which comprises food articles and food products, dipped marginally to 8.58 per cent last month, from 8.66 per cent September. Meanwhile, the Output Producer Price Index grew by 12.06 per cent year-on-year in October. According to the data, cumulative WPI inflation for April to October period stood at 10.14 per cent, compared with a contraction of 0.3 per cent during the corresponding period of the previous financial year.

. India has been re-elected to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Council for the 2027-2030 term, during the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha, Qatar. The 48-member ITU Council acts as the organization’s governing body between quadrennial Plenipotentiary Conferences. It oversees global telecommunication policies, strategic and financial plans, and working groups.Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said, our resounding victory in the ITU Council elections reflects the trust and confidence the global community reposes in India’s growing capabilities and its commitment to shaping the future of telecommunications and digital connectivity.Department of Telecommunications reaffirmed India’s commitment to building a connected, inclusive, secure and sustainable digital future for all.On October 8, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said India’s telecom sector has evolved beyond networks, spectrum and internet speeds, with mobile connectivity emerging as a key enabler of governance and access to public services.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited the Khalsa Diwan Gurudwara in Manila today and led the foundation-laying ceremony for the redevelopment of the Gurudwara in the presence of Panch Pyare. On the occasion, several dignitaries, including Senator Francis Joseph Escudero and Mayor of Manila City, Francisco Isko Moreno, were present.Originally established in 1901 and formally organised in 1903, the institution was registered as Khalsa Diwan in 1924. The Khalsa Diwan Gurudwara holds the unique distinction of being the oldest Gurudwara in the Philippines. It continues to play an important role through its spiritual, cultural and philanthropic activities for the Sikh and other communities in Manila.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow.The Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep during the next two days. Similar conditions are expected over Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura tomorrow.Meanwhile, the weather agency has forecast mist and shallow fog at most places of Delhi during the morning hours tomorrow.The air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the ‘ Very Poor’ category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index was recorded at 303 as of 7 PM today.

. In Badminton, India’s Lakshya Sen has stormed into the men’s singles final of the Kumamoto Masters Japan after defeating Indonesia’s sixth-seeded Alwi Farhan 21-12, 15-21, 21-11 in a thrilling three-game semifinal today. The 25-year-old Indian shuttler will now face Japan’s Koki Watanabe in the title clash tomorrow. Sen dominated the opening game, winning it 21-12. However, Farhan fought back to take the second game 21-15, forcing a decider. The Indian shuttler then produced a strong comeback in the deciding game, winning it convincingly 21-11 to seal his place in the final.

. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will participate in the 4th edition of India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministers’ Dialogue (2+2) during his two-day visit to Japan, beginning tomorrow. During the visit, the Minister will also hold bilateral discussions with his Japanese counterpart.The 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue, to be held in Tokyo, will be co-chaired by the Defence Minister and External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar, along with their Japanese counterpart Shinjiro Koizumi and Toshimitsu Motegi. The dialogue will review the full spectrum of bilateral strategic and defence cooperation, exchange views on regional and global developments, and reaffirm the shared commitment of the two nations to a free, open, inclusive, and rule-based Indo-Pacific.India and Japan share a Special Strategic and Global Partnership rooted in shared democratic values, mutual trust and converging strategic interests. The Ministry said that the upcoming visit aims to further deepen bilateral defence ties and chart the roadmap for enhanced operational and industrial synergy between the two countries.The Defence Ministry said that the bilateral talks between the two Defence Ministers will be their third meeting this year. They will also deliberate on advancing defence equipment and technology collaboration, maritime security, enhancing the scale and complexity of joint exercises across all three services, and deepening industrial partnerships. The meeting will further build the momentum from their interactions in New Delhi in August and on the margins of the ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus in Cebu in October this year.

. The Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority (IEPFA), Securities and Exchange Board of India and Market Infrastructure Institutions will orgaise a day-long Niveshak Shivir in New Delhi tomorrow. Ministry of Corporate Affairs said that the initiative is designed to help investors and shareholders resolve issues related to unclaimed dividends, shares transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund and other claimant-related grievances. Through the Shivir, IEPFA aims to facilitate the recovery of unclaimed dividends and shares held for six to seven years with companies, on-the-spot KYC updation and nomination-related services. It will also provide immediate assistance and resolution of pending IEPFA claim-related issues. The Niveshak Shivir model promotes direct, intermediary-free engagement between investors, companies, and Registrars and Transfer Agents.The Niveshak Shivir forms part of IEPFA’s nationwide investor outreach and awareness programme, aimed at strengthening financial literacy, enhancing transparency, and simplifying the process of reclaiming unclaimed investments.

. NITI Aayog today launched the workshop, titled ‘Leadership as Mission’, at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. This is the first workshop of the series of five National Workshops which will be launched in days to come to draw lessons from Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s twenty-five years as Head of Government. The other four workshops focus on themes: Governance as Delivery, Development as Inclusion, Civilisational Identity and India’s Global Role. The series will continue until October next year.The first workshop, launched today, features first-hand accounts of key governance initiatives, including the reconstruction of Kutch following the 2001 earthquake, India’s response to COVID-19, the Lakhpati Didi initiative and the opening up of the space sector. The workshop was attended by Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister Dr P K Mishra and NITI Aayog Vice Chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri.Addressing the gathering, Mr Lahiri said that Viksit Bharat at 2047 is a program for systematic target-driven economic transformation. He said that by the centennial of country’s independence in 2047, India aims at a GDP of 30 to 40 trillion-dollar economy. Niti Aayog Vice-Chairman underlined that the goal requires a sustained annual real GDP growth rate of 7 to 10 per cent. He said that the vision of Viksit Bharat aims to build a state-of-the-art digital public infrastructure to go beyond basic financial inclusion toward livelihood, productivity, decentralised credit access, AI integration and MSME market expansion. He added that it also aims at 100 percent literacy, net zero carbon emission and life expectancy exceeding 80 years and focuses on the youths, the poor, women and farmers.In his address,  Dr PK Mishra highlighted that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership over the past 25 years centred on three key principles of integrity, teamwork and technology. He said that the workshop will benefit people from diverse backgrounds, officers who will contribute to nation-building for the next two decades or more, youth, students, and community members. He emphasised that a mission goes beyond a programme, with clear goals, defined timelines, public participation and accountability at every level, transforming government initiatives into people’s movements.Dr Mishra noted that 25 years of governance under Mr Modi, first as Gujarat Chief Minister and later as Prime Minister, offer valuable lessons from large-scale public initiatives.  He emphasised that the success of these initiatives reflects the collective efforts of officials, professionals, frontline workers and citizens, whose experiences serve as a valuable national asset for shaping India’s future governance. Dr Mishra said that the Prime Minister’s philosophy of leadership calls for a clear vision, courage for its execution, empathy and inclusion to ensure that development reaches every citizen.He said that India’s response to COVID-19 pandemic demonstrates that a democracy can act with speed and scale when the whole of government and whole of society move together, transparency in stages of delivery, and when citizens trust the state enough to participate. The Principal Secretary said that the Lakhpati Didi initiative focused on how empowerment is the most enduring form of development. Dr Mishra also underlined that the opening of the space sector under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasised the value of farsighted reform. He said that the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 has transformed what the nation expects from public service, from process compliance to outcome delivery, and from incremental improvement to accelerated transformation.

. Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya and Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy today unveiled the logo and mascot for the 8th edition of the Khelo India Youth Games. The Games will be held across six cities in Telangana from 11th to 22nd of next month.Addressing the gathering, Dr Mandaviya said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has placed special emphasis on connecting the youth with sports and making sports an integral part of the country’s development vision. He said various sporting events, including the Khelo India Youth Games, Khelo India Beach Games, Winter Games and Tribal Games, are being organised under the Khelo India initiative to encourage greater participation of young people in sports.Speaking on the occasion, Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy said events such as the Khelo India Youth Games would help advance the Prime Minister’s vision of a Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat by encouraging young people to stay away from substance abuse and other social challenges.Both Dr Mandaviya and Mr Reddy expressed their gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his guidance and support in organising the Khelo India Youth Games in Telangana.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said around eight thousand athletes and participants are expected to take part in the Games. The 8th edition will feature 29 disciplines, including 27 competitive sports and two demonstration events.

. Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, has called for moving the global just transition agenda from dialogue and exchange of experiences towards practical, country-driven implementation. Addressing the Fourth Annual High-Level Ministerial Roundtable on Just Transition under the UAE Just Transition Work Programme at UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya (Türkiye) yesterday, the Minister reiterated India’s commitment to an inclusive and equitable global transition that leaves no one behind.Noting that there can be no one-size-fits-all approach, he cited India’s sub-national heat action and disaster management plans, which address vulnerabilities of workers and communities, as well as the country’s renewable energy expansion that seeks to combine low-carbon development with affordable energy access. These examples underline the need to integrate just transition considerations across adaptation, livelihoods and development planning, he added.The Minister underlined the need for clearly defined and complementary roles for the UAE Just Transition Work Programme and the proposed Just Transition Mechanism. While the Work Programme should continue to provide a platform for dialogue and exchange of experiences, the Mechanism should facilitate practical support through technical assistance, capacity-building and cooperation, translating the learnings from ongoing discussions into action, he stated.

. Most Asian stock markets ended in negative zone today. Taiwan’s Taiex plunged six per cent,  South Korea’s Kospi lost 3.6 per cent, Japan’s Nikkei 225 shed 2.4 per cent, Singapore’s Strait Times index as well as China’s Shanghai Composite fell 0.9 per cent. In contrast, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng gained half a per cent.On the economic front, Japan’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) estimates for the third quarter contracted at an annualized rate of 0.1 per cent, according to the data released by the government.In European markets, London’s FTSE 100 rose 0.4 per cent, while Germany’s DAX dipped marginally, when reports last came in.

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today chaired the second Pre-Budget Consultation meeting with experts from agriculture and rural development sectors ahead of the forthcoming General Budget 2027-28 in New Delhi. The Pre-Budget consultation meeting was also attended by Secretaries of Department of Economic Affairs, Anuradha Thakur, Secretary of Department of Fisheries, Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi and senior officials of Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.Earlier in the day, the Finance Minister chaired the first Pre-Budget Consultation with leading economists in connection with the upcoming Union Budget 2027-28, in New Delhi. The meeting was also attended by Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs, Anuradha Thakur and Chief Economic Adviser, Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran and senior officers from the Department.The Finance Ministry conducts several pre-Budget consultation meetings annually with experts, industry leaders, economists, and state officials. The deliberations seek to ensure the Union budget reflects diverse perspectives and addresses key economic priorities.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended over half a per cent higher today. The Sensex climbed 512 points to close at 82,105. The Nifty rose 147 points to settle at 25,291. However, the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, underperformed the frontline indices. The Midcap 100 index fell half a per cent, and the Smallcap 100 index lost 1.1 per cent.

. The International Cricket Council (ICC) Board has approved the windows for major men’s events until 2035, confirming that India will host the 2029 Champions Trophy and co-host the 2031 ODI World Cup with Bangladesh.The 2029 Champions Trophy will be held in India from 9th to 28th of October, while the 2031 ODI World Cup will take place from 9th October to 23rd November, jointly hosted by India and Bangladesh.The ICC also announced the dates for tournaments beyond 2031, although the host nations are yet to be confirmed. The schedule covers major events from the 2028 T20 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand to the 2035 ODI World Cup.The 2028 T20 World Cup will run from October 12 to  November 12. The next edition will be held in 2030, with England, Scotland and Ireland jointly hosting the tournament. The 2032 and 2034 editions are also scheduled, but their venues are yet to be announced.Meanwhile, the World Test Championship (WTC) Final will continue to be held every two years in June until 2035. England will host the 2029 and 2031 finals, while the hosts for the 2033 and 2035 editions are yet to be decided.

. President Droupadi Murmu today said that India has made significant progress in controlling malaria in recent years. The President said this while addressing the Golden Jubilee celebrations of the Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Malaria Research in New Delhi. She said that good healthcare, advanced medications, mosquito control campaigns, and community partnership have played an effective role in containing malaria cases. She said that malaria cases and deaths in the country have declined by nearly 80 per cent in the last 10 years and the number of high-burden districts decreased from 155 to 33.President Murmu added that 160 districts reported zero malaria cases during 2022 to 2025. President Murmu called for sustained research, public awareness and active community participation to achieve the goal of malaria elimination in India. The President highlighted that the Indian Council of Medical Research – National Institute of Malaria Research has played an important role in India’s fight against the disease.Speaking on the occasion, Union Health Minister J P Nadda expressed confidence in achieving the global malaria elimination vision by 2030. He said sustained research and effective public health participation would play a critical role in achieving the target. The Minister further said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi the government remains committed to strengthening the health sector and eliminating diseases across the country.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that the Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’ over central parts of South and adjoining West Central Bay of Bengal has moved north-northwestwards and is likely to intensify into a Severe Cyclonic Storm around evening today.Thereafter, it is likely to move northwestwards and intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm around Thursday morning. IMD said that continuing to move northwestwards, it is likely to cross Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni, on Friday as a very severe cyclonic storm. The Met Department has advised the fishermen not to venture into Northwest, Southwest and West Central Bay of Bengal till 20th of this month.The Weather Agency has forecast heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu Puducherry and Karaikal till tomorrow. IMD has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Andhra Pradesh and Andaman and Nicobar Islands during the next two to three days. It said that dense fog conditions are very likely to continue over Delhi, Haryana Chandigarh and Punjab during the next two to three days. Dense fog conditions are also likely to continue over Uttar Pradesh till tomorrow.Meanwhile, air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the Poor category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded at 214 as of 1 PM today.

. In the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by 32 paise to trade at 93.93 rupees against the US dollar. The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 103.53 in intra-day trade.

. In Mizoram, three-day Leitlangpui Music Festival is underway in south Mizoram’s Lunglei town, bringing together established musicians, emerging bands and local entrepreneurs to showcase the state’s musical heritage and promote tourism. Organised by the Ministry of Tourism and Mizoram Tourism department, the festival began yesterday at Lena Stadium at Serkawn under the theme “Music Comes Home to Serkawn”. The festival seeks to connect that legacy with contemporary musicians and emerging talent.Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Tourism Minister Lalnghinglova Hmar said music was an inseparable part of Mizoram’s cultural identity and Serkawn held a special place in the state’s musical history. The minister said that the government aimed to take Mizoram’s music and cultural heritage to national and international audiences while creating opportunities for young artists, entrepreneurs and local communities. The festival features performances by established and emerging Mizo musicians.The second day includes a band competition with 10 finalists from Aizawl, Lunglei, Nagaland and Assam, while winners of the previous two editions, Swordtune and Knot, are also scheduled to perform. The final day will feature performances by several Mizo artists and bands, followed by the minister’s address and a fireworks display.

. In Football, India registered a 2-1 victory over Bhutan in the semifinal of the SAFF Championship in Dhaka today. With this win India booked their place in the final and keeping their pursuit of a record-extending 10th title alive. Vishnu PV opened the scoring for India in the ninth minute, while captain Chinglensana Singh Konsham doubled the lead in the 27th minute. Kinzang Tashi Tobden’s scored only goal for Bhutan in the 48th minute. India will now face the winner of the other semifinal between Bangladesh and Pakistan in the final on November 17.

. In Football, defending champions India will take on Pakistan in the final of the SAFF Championship at the National Stadium in Dhaka, Bangladesh, today. India will be aiming to secure their 10th overall SAFF Championship title and make history by winning the tournament for the third consecutive time. The Blue Tigers booked their place in the final after defeating Bhutan 2-1 in the semi-final on Saturday.Pakistan, meanwhile, will be making their first-ever appearance in a SAFF Championship final. The two sides have met 30 times in senior internationals, with India winning 17 matches, Pakistan four and nine ending in draws. Today’s clash will, however, be their first meeting in a senior SAFF Championship final.India are the most successful team in the tournament’s history, having won a record nine titles, and they are the favourites to lift the trophy once again.

. India’s overall unemployment rate declined by 0.3 per cent to 4.9 per cent in October on an annual basis. According to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation’s periodic labour force survey bulletin, the rural unemployment rate fell to 4.2 per cent and urban unemployment rate decreased to 6.7 per cent last month. Worker Population Ratio (WPR) increased by half a per cent to 53 per cent in October on an annual basis. WPR in rural areas increased to 58.4 per cent last month, while in urban areas it remained unchanged at 50.5 per cent on a year-on-year basis. Among female, WPR rose to 33.3 per cent in October. Meanwhile, the male WPR remained largely unchanged at 73.7 per cent over the same period.The overall Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) among persons of age 15 years and above grew by 0.3 per cent to 55.7 per cent last month on an annual basis.

. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold declined 0.6 per cent to 1,34,971 rupees per 10 grams. Meanwhile, silver shed 4.4 per cent to 1,70,251 rupees per kilogram according to the closing rates of India Bullion and Jewellers Association.

. In Men’s Cricket, India defeated Pakistan by one wicket in a thrilling final to clinch the Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup title in Muscat, Oman, today. Lower-order batters Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva played sensational knocks to help India snatch victory from the jaws of defeat and successfully chase down a challenging target of 338 runs. Needing three runs off the final delivery, Mohit Ulva struck a boundary to seal India’s record-extending ninth title. Mohit remained unbeaten on 49 off just 26 deliveries, while Manal Chauhan contributed a valuable 47 off 32 balls. Skipper Lakshya Raichandani also played a crucial role with a brilliant 80-run knock. Mohit Ulva was named player of the match, while Aaryavir Sehwag was awarded player of the tournament.Earlier, opting to bat first, Pakistan posted 337 for 9 in their allotted 50 overs. Their innings was powered by a century from Usman Khan and half-centuries from Abdul Qadir and Farhan Yousaf. For India, Kavya Patel led India’s bowling attack, claiming four wickets.President Droupadi Murmu congratulated Team India on winning the Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup. In a social media post, the President lauded the young champions for displaying exceptional skill, determination, and composure throughout the closely contested final match.Prime Minister Narendra Modi  has also congratulated the young cricketers. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that today is an outstanding day for Indian cricket. He said that their success will inspire several youngsters.Congratulating young cricketers, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said that the determination, firm resolve, and excellent sportsmanship they demonstrated on the pitch were a masterclass in India’s cricketing excellence.

. The Cyclonic Storm Akvan has remained stationary during the past nine hours about 610 km east of Chennai over Central parts of South and adjoining West Central Bay of Bengal. True to its name, its massive structure extends to 630 km northeast of Trincomalee in Srilanka, 670 km southeast of Visakhapatnam in Andhra and 790 km South of Godalpur in Odisha. It is likely to move north-northwestward this evening and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm on the 19th .On the 20th around noon, AKVAN is likely to turn into a very severe cyclonic storm and cross Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni fiercely with a wind speed ranging from 120 to 130 kmph gusting up to 145 kmph. Light to moderate and heavy rains have been predicted at isolated places over North Tamil Nadu till the 19th of this month.

. The Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare will conduct the month-long fifth nation-wide Digital Life Certificate (DLC) campaign across the country from the 1st of next month. Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Ministry said that this is the biggest-ever DLC Campaign undertaken by the Ministry. Electronics and Information Technology Ministry and UIDAI will provide technical support during this campaign. The Ministry said that the initiative will be adopted with a Whole of Government approach with the objective of reaching pensioners in the remotest corners of the country with focus on Face Authentication Technology. The Ministry said that face Authentication for Digital Life Certificate is a seamless and fast mode for DLC generation which can be used both on Android and Apple devices, making it easy and convenient for elderly Pensioners.The Campaign will be conducted in an Utsav mode by offering a bouquet of services such as Health Check-ups and Aadhaar updation for pensioners. Doorstep services to be provided to pensioners based on their requirement.

. Weekly flight from Chennai to Yangon, Myanmar has been cancelled both ways today due to the advent of Cyclone Akvan in the Bay of Bengal. Over 144 passengers who arrived from Ramanthapuram and Tirunelveli had to return to their home town as the next flight will depart next week.

. Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare  Shivraj Singh Chouhan has announced that India’s total horticulture production is expected to reach over three thousand and 869  lakh tonnes in 2025-26. Mr Singh today released the Third Advance Estimates of area and production of horticultural crops for the year 2025-26.Talking to the media in New Delhi, Mr Chouhan said that the projected production is 161.77 lakh tonnes more than the total horticulture production of nearly  3 thouand 707 lakh tonnes recorded in 2024-25, which reflects a growth of 4.36 percent. Mr Chouhan said the significant increase in horticulture production reflects the hard work of India’s farmers and the impact of the farmer-friendly policies of the government.The Minister noted that the total area under horticultural crops in 2025-26 is estimated at neary  297.21 lakh hectares, compared with 301.36 lakh hectares in 2024-25. He said, despite the decline in cultivated area, production is projected to increase across fruits, vegetables, flowers, plantation crops, and aromatic and medicinal plants.Mr Chouhan informed that fruit production is estimated to rise from over one thousand and 176 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 to over one thousand and 230 lakh tonnes in 2025-26, showing an increase of increase of 54.18 lakh tonnes  or  4.60 percent. The improved output is primarily attributed to better production of banana, mango, papaya, apple, pomegranate and jackfruit. According to the third  advance estimates, vegetable production is also projected to rise by 4.35 percent , from nearly  two thousand and  178 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 to over two thousand 272.68 lakh tonnes in 2025-26. Potato production is estimated at 655.70 lakh tonnes, up by nearly 12 percent  from  previous year production while tomato production is projected to increase from around 206 lakh tonnes to  over 214 lakh tonnes. Mr Chouhan said that onion production is estimated at 288.96 lakh tonnes.

. India has strongly objected to Turkiye’s exclusion of New Delhi and several other countries from consultations on a United Nations resolution concerning cooperation with the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC). India voted against the draft resolution in the UN General Assembly, which was adopted with 112 votes in favour, six against and 39 abstentions. India’s Deputy Permanent Representative at the UN Ambassador Yojna Patel criticised the lack of transparency and inclusivity in the negotiation process.

. In Football, defending champions India will aim for a 10th overall and third successive SAFF Championship title when they face Pakistan in the summit clash of the tournament in Dhaka tomorrow.India had defeated Bhutan by 2-1 in the semifinals to make their way into the final on Saturday. The Blue Tigers have won a record nine titles -in 1993, 1997, 1999, 2005, 2009, 2011, 2015, 2021 and 2023 and they are the favourites to lift the trophy once again. India’s head coach for 2026 SAFF Championship, Naushad Moosa, has expressed satisfaction with the team’s progress to another final, crediting the collective effort of the players and support staff. Pakistan will be appearing in their first ever SAFF Championship final.

. The 45th Indian International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 will begin tomorrow at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Talking to media, Chairman of India Trade Promotion Organisation, Jawed Ashraf said that this year the focus is on three key aspects that are enhancing the visitor experience, showcasing innovations and highlighting India’s rich heritage. He said that visitors can book tickets online through the IITF 2026 mobile application, which is integrated with the DMRC’s Sarthi app. Mr Ashraf informed that shuttle bus services will operate from several metro stations, including Mandi House, connecting visitors to all entry gates of the venue. Visitors can also reach Bharat Mandapam through app-based taxis, private vehicles and public transport. He added that parking facilities for around three thousand vehicles have been arranged, along with designated waiting areas for app-based taxis. Special facilities, including wheelchair assistance will also be available for senior citizens to ensure a comfortable and convenient experience.

. Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush of Diwali and Chhath Puja, with extensive crowd management preparations underway at several railway stations. Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing dedicated passenger holding areas, known as Yatri Suvidha Kendras, at major railway stations across the country. This is being done to streamline passenger movement and ease congestion during periods of heavy footfall, including the festive season. The Yatri Suvidha Kendras, or Passenger Holding Areas, are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers. Our correspondent reports that the facilities have been designed to ensure orderly passenger movement and provide a comfortable waiting environment.The holding areas have been designed to accommodate passengers before they proceed to the platform area. Talking to Akashvani News, Northern Railway CPRO  said that at New Delhi Railway station, a holding area is available for both reserved and unreserved classes. He said additional RPF personnel have also been deployed at Railway stations to facilitate passengers.At Anand Vihar Terminal, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra has 14 ticket counters, 16 CCTV cameras, four electronic display boards and seating for 20 passengers. The facility also has separate toilet facilities for male and female passengers, a Divyangjan toilet, an RO plant, 11 HVLS fans and a public announcement system. The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms, in circulating areas and at station approaches by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing.

. Political tensions in Bangladesh appear to be spilling beyond the country’s borders, with clashes erupting between supporters of the Awami League and the National Citizen Party (NCP), leaving at least four people injured in London yesterday.According to media reports, the clashes took place on a road in central London following a reception organised for NCP Convener and Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam, who is on a week-long visit to the United Kingdom.Eyewitnesses and organisers said Awami League supporters gathered outside the venue and threw eggs and water bottles at guests arriving for the event. Tensions escalated after the programme, leading to clashes and chasing between the two groups for around 20 minutes.The injured were admitted to local hospitals, while London police reportedly baton-charged several times to restore order.The incident comes days after an alleged attempt by Awami League supporters to confront Nahid Islam at Cambridge University, raising concerns that Bangladesh’s domestic political rivalries are increasingly extending into the Bangladeshi diaspora abroad.

. Labour unrest continues in Bangladesh’s major industrial areas, with garment workers staging fresh protests in Gazipur, Savar, Ashulia and parts of Dhaka today, disrupting road communications and factory operations.According to Bangladeshi media reports, workers blocked the Dhaka-Mymensingh and Dhaka-Aricha highways at several points, affecting traffic between the capital and northern districts. Demonstrators are demanding an increase in the monthly minimum wage to 30,000 taka.In Gazipur, hundreds of workers took to the streets, blocked roads and clashed with police. Reports said 31 factories declared closures amid the unrest. Police fired sound grenades to disperse protesters, while incidents of vehicle vandalism were also reported.In Savar’s Hemayetpur, workers blocked roads and set tyres on fire, prompting police and Border Guard Bangladesh personnel to intervene. Tear gas shells and sound grenades were reportedly used to disperse demonstrators.Protests were also reported in Ashulia and Mirpur, where workers blocked roads and disrupted traffic.Workers’ anger has reportedly intensified following the postponement of a wage board meeting at which they had expected an announcement on the new minimum wage.Additional police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed in the affected areas as authorities attempt to restore normal traffic and industrial operations.

. In Men’s Cricket, India defeated Pakistan by one wicket in a thrilling final to clinch the Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup title in Muscat, Oman, yesterday. Lower-order batters Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva played sensational knocks to help India snatch victory from the jaws of defeat and successfully chase down a challenging target of 338 runs.Needing three runs off the final delivery, Mohit Ulva struck a boundary to seal India’s record-extending ninth title. Mohit remained unbeaten on 49 off just 26 deliveries, while Manal Chauhan contributed a valuable 47 off 32 balls. Skipper Lakshya Raichandani also played a crucial role with a brilliant 80-run knock. Mohit Ulva was named Player of the Match, while Aaryavir Sehwag was awarded Player of the Tournament.Earlier, opting to bat first, Pakistan posted 337 for 9 in their allotted 50 overs. Their innings was powered by a century from Usman Khan and half-centuries from Abdul Qadir and Farhan Yousaf. For India, Kavya Patel led the bowling attack, claiming four wickets.Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah have congratulated the Indian team on its victory in the Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup 2026.

. The Char Dham Yatra for this year has concluded with the closure of Badrinath Dham yesterday for the winter season with full rituals, Vedic chanting and religious traditions. A large number of devotees were present on the Badrinath temple premises on the occasion of the closure of the portals.Before the doors were closed, prescribed religious rituals were performed inside the temple. According to tradition, Goddess Lakshmi was consecrated inside the sanctum sanctorum, following which the portals of Lord Badri Vishal were closed for the winter season. More than 65 lakh pilgrims from across the country and abroad visited the four sacred shrines during this year’s Char Dham Yatra, while over 23 lakh pilgrims visited Badrinath Dham alone, marking a new milestone.Earlier on November 11, the portals of Kedarnath Dham were ceremonially closed for the winter season with more than 19.20 lakh devotees visiting the Himalayan shrine during this year’s pilgrimage season.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today highlighted the growing partnership between India and ASEAN and called for greater cooperation to ensure peace, stability and prosperity in the Indo-Pacific region. He was addressing the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit in Manila, Philippines.Prime Minister Modi congratulated Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on his successful chairship of ASEAN.He said that this was his 13th interaction with ASEAN leaders in this format and said India’s Act East policy had given India-ASEAN relations new momentum and depth over the past several years.Highlighting the expansion of bilateral cooperation, PM Modi said the partnership, built on shared culture and heritage, was now expanding into new areas such as digital technologies, defence and space.He further stated that since 2014, India and ASEAN had undertaken more than 100 initiatives to strengthen people-to-people ties.He added that more than 250 quick-impact projects had been launched, while over 10,000 scholarships had been provided for skill development.The Prime Minister further said that direct flights between India and nine ASEAN countries, along with growing tourism, reflected the close ties between the two sides.He said the summit’s theme,” Navigating Our Future Together”, held particular significance in the current global context. He emphasised that India and ASEAN together represented about one-fourth of the world’s population and that their future should be shaped through cooperation rather than competition.He added that India and ASEAN possessed the capabilities and shared resolve to make the region a symbol of peace and stability.PM Modi also noted that this was his third visit to an ASEAN country this year, reflecting the special importance ASEAN held for India.He said India’s development and ASEAN’s prosperity were closely interconnected, adding that the ASEAN Community Vision 2045 and India’s vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047 could play an important role in achieving shared aspirations.The Prime Minister observed that over the past twelve years, India and ASEAN had given their partnership fresh momentum and stressed the need to work together to chart a new course for the future of the region.Reaffirming India’s commitment, PM Modi said the country’s support for ASEAN unity and ASEAN centrality would remain unwavering.Expressing confidence in the outcome of the summit, he said the meeting would elevate the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to new heights and contribute to building a secure, inclusive and prosperous Indo-Pacific.Later, the Prime Minister attended the 21st East Asia Summit, which brought together leaders of ASEAN member states and its eight dialogue partners to discuss regional and international issues.Earlier, PM Modi visited the Khalsa Diwan Gurudwara in Manila today and led the foundation-laying ceremony for the redevelopment of the Gurudwara in the presence of Panj Pyare.

. The nationwide ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ campaign has concluded with 536 Yuva Samvads conducted across 31 States and Union Territories. The campaign organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) reached over one lakh young people and involved more than 5000 Youth Icons. The campaign brought discussions on electoral awareness to colleges and educational institutions across the country. It encouraged young people, particularly first-time voters, to understand their voting rights and electoral procedures and participate responsibly in democracy.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the campaign witnessed participation by Governors, Union Ministers, State Ministers, Members of Parliament and other public representatives. It added that sports personalities and youth icons from the sporting community also participated in programmes, sharing their experiences and encouraging youth participation in sports.The Yuva Samvads provided young participants with opportunities to seek clarity on electoral procedures, discuss voting rights and civic responsibilities, and interact directly with public representatives and Youth Icons.

. Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr Virendra Kumar today inaugurated the Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat, INA in New Delhi this evening. The Mela will provide a dedicated marketing platform to artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities to showcase and market their products to a wider audience. Speaking on the occassion, Dr Kumar said the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022 and more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and market their products.  The Minister said that with approximately 150 stalls for participating male and female artisans to showcase their handicraft and handloom products under Bharat TULIP and Purple Fest, the initiative brings traditional artisans, creative talent and persons with disabilities together on a common platform to encourage wider market access and equal opportunities for participation.  The Mela will remain open to visitors until 15th of this month.

. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s dedicated Health Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 in New Delhi is showcasing its flagship health programmes and public healthcare initiatives. The theme of this year’s Health Pavilion is Yuva Bharat, Swasth Bharat, highlights preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles and youth participation in building a healthier nation. The Pavilion was inaugurated by NITI Aayog Member, Dr M Srinivas, in the presence of Health Secretary, Punya Salila Srivastava.Addressing the gathering, Dr. Srinivas emphasised on preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyle choices to address rising burden of Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs) and lifestyle-related health conditions. He also highlighted the importance of public awareness, early detection and timely medical intervention in preventing and managing NCDs. Outlining the benefits of Health Pavilion, Dr. Srinivas said that it offers a valuable opportunity for citizens to learn about common health risks, understand preventive measures and familiarise themselves with various Government healthcare programmes and services. He also encouraged visitors to actively participate in the Pavilion’s activities and use the opportunity to enhance their understanding of health and well-being.The Ministry noted that in the Pavilion 39 stalls representing 24 national health programmes and organisations showcase Government’s healthcare initiatives, achievements and services. The Ministry also highlighted that a dedicated TB stall has been established to raise awareness about tuberculosis and TB screening is being conducted using AI-enabled handheld X-ray technology. The Pavilion also included interactive activities, live cpr demonstrations, health awareness sessions and dedicated kids’ zone to engage visitors and promote healthy living. The Ministry said that the Pavilion provides an important platform to connect directly with citizens, showcase the Government’s wide-ranging healthcare initiatives and promote greater public awareness about preventive healthcare, early diagnosis and healthier lifestyles.

. Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) and the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus (NASB) signed the Second Programme of Cooperation for the period 2027-2029 to further strengthen bilateral scientific and technological partnership between India and Belarus. The Programme of Cooperation was signed during a meeting between Director General, CSIR, Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, and Deputy Chairman of the Praesidium of NASB, Dr. A. V. Trukhanov in New Delhi yesterday.The Science and Technology Ministry said that the agreement provides a renewed framework for expanding bilateral scientific collaboration, facilitating joint research and development initiatives and strengthening linkages between research institutions and scientists of both countries. It is expected to provide an impetus to collaborative research, technology development, knowledge exchange and innovation-driven partnerships through focused cooperation in mutually identified areas of science and technology.The two institutions also propose to launch the Second Joint Call for Research, Development and Innovation Proposals from 27th of this month and invite proposals from researchers and scientists of both countries for undertaking collaborative research projects in mutually identified priority areas.

. Three major works of India’s literary and intellectual heritage including Kalhana’s Rajatarangini, the Mahabharata and Kautilya’s Arthashastra have been included in UNESCO’s Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the register held in Jakarta, Indonesia. With this recognition, India’s total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six. The three works represent different aspects of India’s knowledge traditions. Rajatarangini is a historical account of Kashmir, the Mahabharata explores Dharma, duty and human values, while Arthashastra deals with governance, diplomacy and statecraft. This recognition is a matter of pride for India’s civilisational continuity, its rich knowledge traditions and its contribution to the world. The development was announced by Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA),  Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi which played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.

. India and Egypt today agreed to work towards finalising the Terms of Reference (ToR) for a proposed bilateral trade agreement to strengthen economic ties between the two countries. At the 7th India-Egypt Joint Trade Committee meeting in Cairo, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said, the two countries could enhance cooperation in several sectors, including pharmaceuticals and healthcare, engineering and automobiles, agriculture, digitisation, fintech and museums.Highlighting opportunities for cooperation in the fintech sector, Mr Goyal said the central banks of both countries were working to promote trade in local currencies. He also proposed linking India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) with Egypt’s digital payment systems. The Minister said a joint team from both countries would work in a time-bound manner to finalise the Terms of Reference for the proposed trade agreement. He said the agreement could take bilateral economic relations to a new level by expanding trade and investment and promoting a more comprehensive partnership across various sectors, including education. The Egyptian delegation was led by Mohamed Farid Saleh, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt.Mr Goyal arrived in Cairo yesterday on a two-day visit aimed at strengthening India-Egypt relations and expanding trade, investment and industrial cooperation. A delegation of more than 130 business leaders and start-ups is accompanying him.

. Akashvani will broadcast the recording of the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, delivered by Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, tonight at 9:30 PM. The recording will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani network on the occasion of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s birth anniversary.Delivering the 67th Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, Mr Chouhan said that Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s vision, determination and leadership laid the foundation for India’s national unity and territorial integrity. He said that Sardar Patel’s efforts to integrate 565 princely states remain a defining chapter in the country’s history. The Minister emphasised that Patel’s vision of a united India continues to inspire the nation through the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’.Mr Chouhan also said that, inspired by Sardar Patel’s firm approach towards national security and his policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, India has responded decisively to threats from across its borders, including through measures such as surgical strikes.As a tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who served as independent India’s first Deputy Prime Minister and Information and Broadcasting Minister, Akashvani has been organising the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture since 1955. Over the years, the annual event has served as a rich repository of thoughts, ideas and perspectives on a wide range of subjects. It has also provided an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of India’s diverse cultural heritage and the various dimensions of its developmental challenges.

. In badminton, India’s Lakshya Sen clinched the men’s singles title at the Kumamoto Masters Japan, defeating Japan’s Koki Watanabe in a thrilling three-game final this morning.Lakshya fought back from a game down to win 13-21, 21-18, 21-14 in one hour and four minutes. With this victory, he became the first Indian shuttler to win the tournament since its inception in 2023.This was Lakshya’s second consecutive BWF Super 500 title, following his triumph at the Hylo Open in Germany earlier this month. It was also his sixth BWF World Tour title and the first time he has won two Tour titles in a single season.The victory earned him 9,200 ranking points, boosting his chances of qualifying for the 2026 BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou.

. The ASEAN member states and India today agreed to strengthen cooperation in disaster management, with a focus on early warning systems, emergency response, disaster preparedness and resilient recovery.The agreement was reached at the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit in Manila, where both sides adopted the ASEAN-India Joint Statement on Cooperation in Disaster Management, seeking to enhance regional coordination and build resilience against natural disasters.Recognising the shared vulnerability of ASEAN countries and India to earthquakes, tsunamis, floods, cyclones, extreme heat and landslides, the two sides stressed the importance of timely humanitarian assistance, effective disaster response mechanisms and stronger regional cooperation.Under the joint statement, ASEAN and India will strengthen coordination among their disaster management agencies, including the ASEAN Committee on Disaster Management (ACDM), the AHA Centre and India’s National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA). They will also expand cooperation on early warning systems through the exchange of satellite data, seismic information and meteorological forecasts.Both sides agreed to conduct joint training programmes, simulation exercises and exchanges of disaster response personnel to improve preparedness and rapid response capabilities. They will also facilitate humanitarian assistance and disaster relief to affected countries upon request or with their consent.The agreement also focuses on sustainable post-disaster recovery, resilient infrastructure and capacity building, with particular attention to women, youth, older persons and persons with disabilities. ASEAN and India will further explore the use of artificial intelligence, machine learning and big data analytics in disaster risk assessment, early warning and response coordination.Relevant ASEAN bodies and their Indian counterparts will identify specific activities to implement the joint statement under the ASEAN-India Plan of Action (2026-2030) and monitor progress through existing mechanisms.The initiative aims to strengthen regional preparedness, improve coordination during emergencies and enhance the resilience of communities across ASEAN and India.

. Vice-President and Rajya Sabha Chairman, C. P. Radhakrishnan today administered the oath of office to Hardeep Singh Puri at Parliament House. Mr Puri has been elected as an Member of the Rajya Sabha from Madhya Pradesh. Union Ministers Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya and Arjun Ram Meghwal, along with other dignitaries, were present on the occasion.

. Indian women’s hockey player and Olympian Lalremsiami Hmar today became the first sportsperson from Mizoram to receive the prestigious Arjuna Award, adding another milestone to her trailblazing career.The 26-year-old was among 17 sportspersons selected for the Arjuna Award 2025 by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports on August 18. President Droupadi Murmu formally presented the honour to her at a ceremony at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi today.Lalremsiami, who hailed from Kolasib in the northern part of Mizoram bordering Assam, took up hockey at a young age.Her talent was spotted by teachers Lallawmawmi, Lalrampari and Lalrothuami, who encouraged her to pursue the sport.Lalremsiami joined the state-run hockey academy at Thenzawl in 2011 at the age of 11, before moving to the National Hockey Academy in New Delhi in 2016.Lalremsiami made her national debut at the Junior Nehru Hockey Tournament in October 2011 and was later selected for India’s Under-18 team for the Asian Cup in 2016.She earned her first senior national team call-up in 2017 and was part of India’s Asia Cup-winning side that year.Since then, she has established herself as a key member of the Indian team, featuring in several major international tournaments, including the Tokyo Olympics 2020, where India finished fourth.She created history in 2018 by becoming the first sportsperson from Mizoram to win an Asian Games medal, helping India secure silver.Her commitment to the national team drew widespread admiration in 2019 when she chose to remain with the squad for the FIH Women’s Series in Japan despite the death of her father, Lalthansanga Zote.India won the tournament and secured qualification for the Tokyo Olympics, making Lalremsiami the first woman from Mizoram to compete at the Olympics.She followed in the footsteps of archer C. Lalremsanga, who represented India at the 1992 Barcelona and 1996 Atlanta Olympics.In 2020, Lalremsiami became the first Indian female hockey player to win the International Hockey Federation’s Women’s Rising Star of the Year award.Her list of achievements has since grown to include a bronze at the 2022 Asian Games, Asian Champions Trophy titles in 2023 and 2024, and gold at the 2026 Asian Games.The Mizoram government had earlier announced a cash reward of Rs 40 lakh each for Lalremsiami and fellow Mizo player Lalthantluangi for their contribution to India’s women’s hockey team that won gold at the Asian Games on October 2.The Arjuna Award now adds another distinction to Lalremsiami’s career, making her the first sportsperson from Mizoram to receive one of the country’s highest honours for sporting achievement.
